notes.title: Update 0.1.7.6c Roof Fixes, Boar Chops & Zone Progress
notes.content:
Fixed a bug where the destruction model of mined rocks was not showing up.

Fixed an issue that prevented projectiles from destroying destructible objects.

A temporary collision check has been added to built houses, allowing roofs to be hidden when entering.

This avoids conflicts with other collisions that prevented roofs from disappearing.

Right now, the roof only appears after the player enters the house once.

This is a temporary workaround until a proper roof setup logic at build completion is added.

Boar death sound volume reduced by 70%.

Fixed a bug where boars and wolves played an extra, incorrect sound on death.

Added Boar Chops as loot and food item. 🥩

The new area’s flora, fauna, and environment are now complete. 🌿🌄

The world map will be adjusted in the coming days.

🛠️ Focus for the next few weeks:

The new area’s with loot filling.

NPCs, dialogues, and quests

New items & crafting recipes

Points of interest and related dungeons

📌 Goal is to check off most of this by the end of the month.

Best regards,
Mark Koch
and as always: Have Fun!

notes.title: Update 0.1.7.6b – Bug Fixes, Boars & Small Improvements
notes.content:
Fixed a bug that prevented building houses.

Item drop physics have been adjusted – they no longer roll or slide as far.

Ranged enemies’ attack speed reduced by 30%.

Some bow skills now have a shorter cast time.

Explosive Arrow now has 50% reduced cooldown.

Shield skills now finally have visual effects.

Added a new animal for more variety in the forests: the wild boar 🐗

🔧 Known issue:
There’s currently a bug with built structures, when trees accidentally respawn inside them. This causes collision issues and prevents roofs from disappearing correctly.
As long as trees are inside the building, the system struggles to display things properly. Once the trees are cut down again, everything works fine.
I'm still looking for a fix for this.

🥩 Wild boars don’t drop their proper loot yet, and their cooking recipes will be added in a future update.

Most of my time is still focused on building the new area.

Best regards,
Mark Koch

and don’t forget: Have Fun!

notes.title: Update 0.1.7.6 – First Area Expansion & Setup for Future Content
notes.content:
This update introduces the first expansion of the game world – it's not fully finished yet, but the foundation is laid. I'm currently working on the flora and fauna, which I plan to complete in the next few days.

Once that's done, I’ll focus on quests, loot, and other content.
New armor, weapons, and matching crafting recipes will come with the new area. I expect to have items and recipes ready by next week.

The new area will also introduce the first “faction” – though I’m still unsure if that’s the right word. Guild doesn’t quite fit, and faction also sounds a bit off.
Let’s call it a thieves’ organization for now.

To avoid false expectations:
There will be no reputation system in the game.
Factions will be kept simple – mostly unlocked via quests, giving access to more quests and specific rewards later on.

It could be possible in the future to have mutually exclusive choices, but I haven’t decided on that yet. That’s a topic for later.

📌 Goal for May:
Add the first faction/organization with the new area.
In parallel, I’ll continue filling the current world with dungeons and quests, especially focusing on the second village, which still needs a lot of content.
That’s the main focus until June.

⚙️ Other tweaks & fixes in this update:

Weather: Thunderstorm chance reduced by 75%.

Bandit voice lines have been removed – they sounded terrible and will be replaced once I can record something better.

Character preview added to the inventory screen – still experimental.

Your character’s level is now displayed beneath the model in the inventory.

Several collision issues and miscellaneous bugs have been fixed.

Best regards,
Mark Koch
and as always – Have Fun! 🎮🔥

notes.title: Finally! Roadmap Plan for Upcoming Content Q2-Q1 2026
notes.content:
I finally managed to put together a Roadmap, something I hadn’t gotten around to since the release. In general, creating the Roadmap is a bit tricky because I’m still unsure about some aspects, like how and when I’ll be able to implement certain things. Additionally, the Roadmap will be somewhat speculative.

For that reason, the Roadmap currently covers only about a year. I will only list things that I can realistically see myself implementing within that time frame. Some aspects, like improving the world map with additional features or other functions, are left out for now.

Of course, more skills are planned, but when and how I’ll implement them, or even what new ideas for skills will arise is difficult to estimate at this point. Therefore, the Roadmap mainly focuses on content in a more "physical" sense essentially, filling the world with substance.

The Roadmap may not be the prettiest, but it should make it clear what I plan to add to the game and when. Below, I will go into more detail about each point.

So don’t forget: Have FUN!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418876/9a64acf1b57ca91d1391b357c040b8d029a22b5c.png[/img]


[b]Expansion of Act 1[/b]

As already mentioned, the priority is on expanding Act 1, and I will try to add a new section every month. Since the largest city, Casandra, is located in Act 1 according to the story I have envisioned for the game, this will be a bit tricky therefore, its gates will not open until the end.

The city itself consists of three levels. Once Act 1 is mostly complete, I will first focus on the first level. At the moment, I am still experimenting with the technical implementation, especially in terms of performance. I hope that there won’t be any major issues, but it could certainly be a challenge. Once the gates to the first level are open, I will have a great opportunity to introduce the story into the game and give it an initial structure.

Act 1 is planned up to level 20. The currently accessible area extends (apart from two Points of Interest Lvl 12 and 15)  up to level 10 and includes two villages. In the second village, Oak Meadow, there are currently only three merchants. Over the next week, I will add more NPCs and start implementing the first quests – step by step.

In general, I plan to create new quests weekly so that the world gradually fills up. The first quests I created last month served as a test run, and I will try to expand the system further, with different outcomes and branching paths. How far I can take this remains to be seen, as I could easily lose track of things.


[b]New Items[/b]

Next on the list is the next tier of iron plate armor. I am still debating whether to divide it into two tiers  (light and heavy plate armor) since there are still ten levels to bridge. In Act 2, the progression would then move towards steel armor.

Additionally, many Named Items are still missing, which I will gradually add. As the name suggests, these items come with their own background stories, associated characters, or puzzles. Similar to the Cassandra artifact armor pieces, but with a deeper connection to the island’s lore. Many of these items will be obtainable through quests or small riddles.

With the introduction of this new item tier, there will, of course, also be new crafting recipes. In general, I want to significantly expand the crafting system.


[b]Dungeons and Puzzles[/b]

Most dungeons, like all side quests, are optional.
Currently, there are:

5 accessible dungeons with enemies

4 smaller dungeons without enemies (mostly caves/cellars where puzzles must be solved to claim rewards)

2 dungeons with enemies that are currently inaccessible (they originate from the early development stages and need to be reworked)

In the currently explorable area, an additional six dungeons are planned, one of which is very well hidden. It serves as a passage to another locked zone. So far, this area only has a rough concept for an item but no planned content yet. Since the entrance is extremely well concealed, I will address it last. I still need to decide what exactly will be found in this zone (Spoiler: apart from a giant tree at the base of which a sword can be found...).

I will also try to hide something in every Point of Interest.
In general, I would like to add many more Points of Interest, as I noticed during testing that the world feels too empty in some areas, and the walking distances are massive, something I honestly didn't expect. To address this, I will add additional small elements to make the world feel richer.


[b]Story Notes
[/b]
For ages, I have planned to add story notes with small narratives and hints for puzzles – some interconnected, others standalone. Unfortunately, I never found the time to write them. It’s always the same thing: "I’ll do it tomorrow..." and that’s been going on for over a year now.

However, my goal is for every location to have a small story or a hint for a puzzle. I should really tackle this next week, it would be a shame if there was a secret door and no one knew how to open it because I forgot to leave a clue. A great example of this is the two dungeons containing Cassandra relics. (Spoiler: Who would even think that breaking specific stones would grant access to a dungeon?)

There are still many planned features, and I apologize that some things are still missing. However, most of the core systems are now functional, which allows me to fully focus on filling the world with content.


[b]New Base Building Structures[/b]

I want to push the building system further and deliver new content as quickly as possible. The next step is stone houses. Right now, it makes no real difference whether a house is built from wood or stone, but at least this will finally give purpose to the 35,000 minable stones I placed over the past weeks.

I also had to shift away from fully player-built houses in favor of pre-designed buildings, simply because I couldn’t figure out a solution for roofs when players construct houses using individual walls, foundations, and so on. I have no idea how to make that work, except perhaps with procedurally generated roofs, but that’s beyond my expertise for now.

Later, I plan to add castles, where it will be possible to individually place each wall, floor, and ceiling.


I hope I haven't forgotten anything important...
But for now, that's the plan. I will do my best to implement everything as quickly as possible, and I hope you will enjoy it. Although, I doubt that anyone has actually read this far.

It’s already almost 1 AM, so don’t forget: Have Fun! ❤️

Best regards,
Mark Koch

notes.title: Quest Fixing
notes.content:
A new fix for the recurring quest bug, plus an update for fast-clicking players!

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to fully fix the issue with the quest reappearing. So here’s another fix.
In my testing, it no longer shows up – at least for me. However, for those who already have it, I can’t remove it anymore.
Since I no longer have an old save file, I wasn’t able to test the fix thoroughly.

The problem is that the quest technically doesn’t exist, making it tricky to remove. I’ve now added an additional method to delete it, but unfortunately, I can’t test it myself. Hopefully, this will finally put an end to this issue. Sorry for the inconvenience!

I plan to finish the quest log system in the next few days, so if the quest still isn’t gone, at least you’ll be able to hide it.

There’s also a small bug in dialogs related to quests for fast-clicking players:
If you complete a task through dialogue and immediately close and restart the dialogue (because you click the NPC too quickly), the quest might not have updated yet – causing you to get stuck in the dialogue since the task is no longer available.

I’ve now reduced the update time from 1 second to 0.5 seconds, hoping that no one clicks that fast. I’ll come up with a permanent solution for ultra-fast clickers and add it in a future update.

If you notice any more bugs, please let me know! I can’t catch everything – four eyes see more than two.

**The demo will be updated later today.**

Best regards, Mark Koch
And don’t forget: Have Fun! 🎮

notes.title: Update 0.1.7.2 – Bug Fixes, Balancing & Learned a Bit of English
notes.content:
Update 0.1.7.2

Right now, I’m trying to create a new trailer. To gather enough video material, I played my game extensively and got my ass kicked constantly... I realized that running back all the time is pretty exhausting.

Additionally, I noticed a few bugs while playing and watching AresLps' stream (much love ❤️), which I want to fix with this update. That’s why this is a slightly bigger patch with bug fixes and balancing adjustments:

Brightness during rain and thunderstorms has been adjusted so it no longer looks like nighttime.
The guy in the tavern has learned English – his dialogue is no longer in German!
I also learned a bit of English – Wulf is now Wolf.
Some collision issues have been fixed.
Ranged weapons now deal more damage.
Some ranged skills now cost less energy.
The pistol now scales with Strength instead of partly with Dex.
Items now have a higher chance to roll Dex for ranged damage scaling.
Two-handed weapon damage has been partially reduced.
The Defence stat on items is no longer a percentage but a fixed value.
The stats of Cassandra Relic armor pieces now work properly.
The light from Cassandra’s Helm has been reworked and hopefully won’t go out anymore.
Enemy damage has been reduced.
The armor value of bandits has been drastically reduced.
Energy potions have been fixed.
Gems now only drop at Level 1 and always stack.
Lockpicks now stack up to 25.
The monster volume for dogs has been lowered.
The bear volume has been significantly reduced.
The chest in the shipwreck for the logbook has been repositioned to be more obvious.
The logbook tutorial questline had a bug where the quest kept reappearing even after completion. From now on, every quest in the questline will be removed upon leaving the first village – even if it shows up again later.
The collision of barrels and crates has been increased so projectiles hit them more easily.
I hope all these changes work as intended. I can only test it properly tomorrow – and hopefully, I won’t be eating dirt as often. At 42, running for miles over and over again is quite tiring. It might be a little too easy now, but we’ll see. Balancing and math are tricky.

Update: Fix ESC is now working on Pause Menu!

Best regards, Mark Koch
And don’t forget: Have fun! 🎮

notes.title: Before you buy!
notes.content:
Since I finally managed to release the game, I want to share a few things with you first. Before you buy, please be aware that this is not a fully finished game. Many features are already implemented, such as base building, crafting, secrets, quests, a dialogue system, and more, but most of them are still quite basic.

I'm still experimenting with some mechanics to find the best way to implement them. Everything works, but it could definitely be better. The UI, in particular, looks pretty terrible – turns out that's not really my talent.

In short: Keep your expectations low. I don’t want anyone to buy the game and end up not having fun. And fun is the most important thing!

Right now, I'm working on adding missing content for the current cave/dungeon over the next few weeks, including secrets and items. At the same time, I’ll be expanding the Area over the next few months to complete Act 1. I’m also planning to create a rough timeline to outline the game's further development.

I highly recommend trying the demo first. It’s not always up to date, but it’s useful for checking performance. Performance is still a tricky issue – a modern graphics card should handle it fine. If you’re not aiming for 4K , your PC should handle it without melting down.

Right now, I’m struggling with shadows and Lumen and looking for ways to optimize performance.

Best regards,
Mark Koch

And don’t forget: Have fun!

notes.title: Where We Stand & Where We’re Headed
notes.content:
If someone had told me a few years ago that I would one day develop my own game, I would probably have thought they were crazy. And now here I am, about to release it in the next few weeks...

Many will surely criticize the fact that the game is coming out so early, and rightly so. But just try testing your own game... especially if you really know every corner of it. Sure, I can look for bugs, but things like balance and gameplay feeling? Difficult. That’s why I depend on every single piece of criticism to adjust the game accordingly. I also expect a lot of critical voices, but I have to be able to handle that as long as they remain constructive.

I have a clear idea of what the game should be and what it should look like later. There is a fixed story about the island where the game takes place, as well as a set story of the hero you play. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418876/773d2d1af20905b69625e230f2e545bad2a28713.png[/img] Still, I’m just a single developer trying to realize my idea without a community or team. That’s also the main reason I decided to release the game now: in the hope that a small community will form, perhaps adding its own touch.

The basic principle of the game is meant to be relatively simple: There is a large world, in this case an island, with numerous dungeons and secrets to explore. You can (with a few exceptions like special places) build your own base almost anywhere and craft unique equipment, potions, buff food, and more. But it won’t be a survival game! You can find unique items, fight hordes of enemies, all the way up to huge world bosses. And it’s all embedded with many small and large stories. I’m definitely not reinventing the wheel here, but I want to create a gaming experience that you rarely encounter in this form, something I’ve missed in many games over the past decades.

Of course, the game won’t be to everyone’s taste and it won’t compare to bigger titles. Let’s not kid ourselves... I’m just a single developer. But I think a key point of the game will be that the world is completely handcrafted and not that generic stuff I see in so many games. The concept of the world and its story is already there, it just needs to be “put into practice.” [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418876/b13bf56467bddbb83fef195335b9aa2227301966.png[/img]

The world will be open world, but with a classic level structure. That means each area has a recommended level requirement. Anyone who likes these types of games will surely have fun here. And that’s exactly what it should be about: fun. That’s why I recommend everyone to play the demo first before buying the game. I don’t want you to get something you end up not enjoying.



[b]Current Status [/b] Act 1 is currently about 50% complete. Actually, I wanted to be much further along by now, but the current area is already quite large and full of puzzles, secrets, and dungeons. I also recently added a dialog system, which I am currently using to create some dialogs to give the game more depth. However, the dialogs should not only contribute to the atmosphere but also have functions, such as assigning tasks. A good example is the blacksmith in the first village: if you bring him iron ore, he expands his shop inventory.

It is uncertain whether I will later give every NPC a dialog, but who knows? In any case, I will add new ones from time to time, depending on what my schedule allows. Complex dialogs take a lot of time, and the more extensive they become, the harder it is for me to keep an overview. At the moment, there are only a handful of dialogs, including the governor in the first village, who is supposed to advance the tutorial quest.

In general, there is still a lot that needs to be expanded in the game. This is especially noticeable with the UI, which, let’s be honest, looks pretty bad right now. Definitely not my strong point! Speaking of the UI: there is already a small skill tree, but it is still far from my final vision. At the moment, it is kept concise on one page, with about 4–5 skills per weapon type. Later, each weapon type will get its own tree. The skill tree and the in-game world map currently perfectly reflect how bad I am at drawing. For the world map, I therefore prefer to use an external program, so that at least you can recognize something and have an easy way to orient yourself.

Because the game world is quite large and I have noticed during my test runs that the walking distances can sometimes be too long, I have built in a small travel option. This works via signposts that stand in every village and that you can also build in your own base. It is very simple: as soon as you have discovered a village, you can travel there from any signpost. In the long run, I could integrate the travel system directly into the map, but until then, the map only serves for orientation.

As for the quests, there will initially only be a handful, mainly focusing on side activities. Since Act 1 is not yet fully developed, my focus remains on designing the world. The main story will only become truly relevant from Act 2 onward, so I need to see how much I can integrate by then.

[b]Enemies and AI[/b] Right now, the enemies in the game can be described with one word: “Dumb” or let’s rather say two words: “Pretty dumb.” Their functions are currently limited to seeing the player, finding the fastest way to them, and attacking. Some already have skills, such as a shout that buffs them or ranged attacks. Anyone expecting complex AI will be disappointed; you can probably find more depth if you look into a well. Some enemies do not even have sounds yet, partly because it is difficult to find license-free sounds. It is even harder to scream monster noises into a microphone at night after work in my apartment...

I have also already tried to create some bosses and put them into the game, some even years ago as first attempts. Maybe I should revise them again before release or remove them altogether. Besides the lack of enemy AI, balance is another big problem: when I do a test run with good equipment that I know inside out, the enemies are no problem. But with poor equipment, I am constantly biting the dust. Finding the right balance will take quite a bit of time, but I hope it will still be doable for new players.

[b]Base Building and Crafting[/b] My goal is to keep the game simple and accessible. And no, I do not mean the mechanics or animations when you chop down a tree and it flies 100 meters... yes, I know, I still have to work on that. I am doing my best! But I do not want the gameplay to feel like work. You should not have to fell hundreds of trees that you have to hack away at forever. Sure, it would be smart to artificially extend the playing time, but you already have to walk enough in my game! So it remains that you can fell a tree in one second and mine stones or ores with one strike.

You will, however, have to invest more time in crafting. Most items you find or craft can be further improved. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418876/e04186085b2adb887c93b59d77b848ee8ad6ab18.png[/img] For example, you can craft or find a normal iron chainmail and upgrade it to a legendary, named version. The same goes for weapons, although there will be only one named item per craftable item. In addition, there will also be randomly legendary or named items to find. At the moment, the scope is still manageable, but in the future it will be expanded to infinity and beyond.

Buff food and potions will help make the game easier for you. If you want it even easier, you can craft powerful gems that can be socketed into equipment, although the resources needed for them are currently still very difficult to obtain.

[b]Performance[/b] Now we come to probably the most important and at the same time the most difficult point: performance. I doubt that anyone has read this far, but I still have to talk about it. My biggest problem is that I only have one single system on which I play and work on the game.

The game runs well on my PC. My computer is not the best, but with an RTX 3070, it is above average compared to many other systems. Originally, I wanted the game to run on a potato or older models. Well, goals and such... Performance is particularly difficult because of Lumen and the associated ray tracing shadows. Some might now be asking, “Why ray tracing shadows?” Well, the game cannot visually keep up with today's titles, but thanks to Lumen, the day-night cycle, and weather effects, the world feels much more alive.

I will try to add an option in the future to disable Lumen. But until then, the system requirements remain as high as they are. If you are not playing in 4K on maximum settings, the game should not fry your graphics card. In general, I recommend everyone to set a fixed FPS with V-Sync to get a stable, smooth image.

Most importantly, never forget:

HAVE FUN! 🎮🔥

notes.title: A somewhat larger update featuring the revisions from the last month.
notes.content:
I think the biggest change in the update is that you can now level up all skills to level 10. Unfortunately, I caused a small bug with this because the prerequisites for the previous skills no longer work. That's what a skill tree is all about: you need to learn the previous skill before you can learn a new one. Since the skill tree is still a bit jumbled and will later be divided into weapon types, I temporarily converted it into a grid structure without skill prerequisites until I fix the issue. The only prerequisite for skills now is the level, and you can just learn the last skill once you reach the required level.

In addition, there are now bandits on the map. They use the same AI, so they’re pretty dumb, but they add some variety. I didn’t create any bandit camps for the spawn points; in the demo, they are present in two locations.

I’ve also updated all the armors with a new skeleton and adjusted the loot in enemy drops accordingly. I haven’t gotten around to the chests yet, but they’ll be updated in the next few days. It’s still possible that old armors may drop in chests.

I think that covers the most important changes. Here's a rough list of the update:

- Added Private Storage Chest in Village
- Added New Items
- Added New Crafting Recipes
- Added Armor Workbench to Build Menu
- Reworked Armors
- Temporarily Reworked Skill Tree
- Added Skill Levels to Skills
- Reworked Enemy Drops and Drop Rates
- Added New Enemy: Bear
- Added New Enemy: Bandits
- Added Bandit Camps
- Improved Performance
- Various Small Adjustments and Fixes

Don't forget: Fun!

notes.title: Demo Build Update
notes.content:
With the Update to v0.008, I've finally to save its state—specifically for harvested resources like stones and trees. This means that these resources are now finite. Once they’re harvested, they won’t respawn when the world is reloaded.

With the current build, building is now possible anywhere, even in the middle of a forest. Only points of interest and dungeons are blocked from construction. I’ve been working on this resource-saving functionality for quite some time, and this current version is the first stable one, as far as I could test it.

In the demo area, there are approximately 60,000 trees and 20,000 stones available to harvest. I have no idea how well the system will handle thousands of trees being chopped down. In my tests, I only harvested about 100 trees or so, and it worked smoothly.

I also tried creating a dedicated demo build, but I abandoned the idea after a few days because it took too much time and effort. This means that, unfortunately, the demo will remain the same size as the full build, with the rest of the game world locked for demo purposes. However, I’ve managed to reduce the overall game size slightly by cleaning up some unnecessary files, saving a few gigabytes.

I apologize for the demo’s size, and I appreciate your understanding.

Wishing you all a Happy New Year—and don’t forget: Have Fun!

notes.title: Main Update for Improved Performance and Elimination of Walking Stutters!
notes.content:
With this update, I aim to improve performance and eliminate the small stutters that occurred while walking. In the future, I plan to introduce enhanced system settings that will hopefully make the game playable on older PCs as well.

Additionally, projectile weapons and their skills have been reintroduced and reworked in this update. Unfortunately, there are still some issues that might cause projectiles to miss their target—so this is still a work in progress.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418876/2ebd54993819cd4c019625da03a4142b4e6e527c.png[/img]
Points of interest have also been added to the world map.

For feedback, you’re always welcome to join my Discord: https://discord.gg/MJYEpS56u4

And don’t forget: Have fun!

notes.title: Perfomence Playtest is Closed!
notes.content:
Originally, my plan was to get the game running smoothly on much older PCs. Unfortunately, this turned out to be much more difficult than expected. I targeted my very old Intel i5 2500 with a GeForce 1060. Well, what can I say? It runs, but it doesn't look nice and smooth is another story. As a result, I'm raising the minimum requirements a bit. Of course, I'll continue to try to improve performance in the future, and there are still some performance-related things I want to implement. But for now, we'll stick with the result, as further improvement would require a much larger overhaul.

For now, I'll focus on expanding the world, dungeons, and features to put together a playable demo by June. For those interested in testing the game to help me with further development, you're welcome to [url=https://discord.gg/B5XNeV8U]join my Discord[/url] server. It's also highly recommended if you want to stay up to date or contribute to the ongoing development. Feel loved and thanks to everyone who helped me during the playtest!

notes.title: The playtest for Lumiel the Awakening is now available!
notes.content: With the start of the first playtest, I want to give you the opportunity to take a first look and, through your feedback, provide a chance to improve the gaming experience. Don't expect too much, as most elements are still under construction. For the playtest, I've created a small area of about 4 km² that will be expanded gradually. The main focus for me initially is on performance. In the coming weeks, a map, more skills, enemies, secrets, dungeons, and the building system will be added step by step. To gain access, please join [url=https://discord.gg/PvrXpnayZD]Discord![/url] without Discord, there will be no activation for the playtest. If some things don't work correctly or at all, or if there are other errors, please excuse me; there's still much for me to learn or test to see how it works. Thank you very much, and have fun!
